Answer: A
Reason: Spontaneous pneumomediastinum (Hamman's syndrome) due to alveolar rupture typically presents with mediastinal air in the absence of pulmonary parenchymal disease or pleural effusion, whereas esophageal rupture (Boerhaave syndrome) is frequently associated with adjacent lung opacification, hydropneumothorax, or pleural effusion. The chest X-ray shows clear lung fields without consolidation or effusion, supporting an alveolar origin over an esophageal one.
